public_contract.signature: bind_migration_inputs(io: InitializationIO, *, paths: tuple[str, ...], limits: ParseLimits) -> InitializationIO
public_contract.effects: Binding is pure. Empty paths returns the original I/O object. Nonempty paths returns a fresh typed adapter preserving every existing public trusted reader, writer, guard, repository, catalog, root and authority-invalidation port; it never mutates the original I/O object.
public_contract.selection: Validate exact tuple/string types, finite count, canonical safe paths, collisions and duplicates before reads or selection retention. Retain one immutable exact selection for the entire operation.
public_contract.capture: Ordinary configured capture remains authoritative. The adapter reads only selected ordinary supplemental files through the existing bounded SnapshotIO metadata/byte seam and retains original bytes as documentation. Identical already-captured paths are coalesced without losing their existing category; conflicting bytes or physical observations fail rather than overwrite prior observations.
public_contract.freshness: Proposal captures include supplemental originals in both CapturedWorkspace and InitializationCapture physical files/metadata. physical_capture and inherited bootstrap/writer/require_same reconstruction use the same adapter and selection. Changes, missing files, links, unsafe paths and conflicting observations are rejected before publication.
public_contract.bounds: Reserve selected-file, path-text, comparison/sort, metadata/retention and aggregate raw-byte/hash-copy work before the relevant traversal, read or allocation. Each bounded read allowance fits the unspent aggregate byte allowance and prepaid byte work. Apply the tighter supplied/profile limits. No sibling-file enumeration or reads and no partial successful capture on exhaustion.
public_contract.profile: No field, template, root, project entry point, ownership or pin in the emitted profile is modified by supplemental capture.
public_contract.caller: service_bootstrap._migrate binds the existing trusted InitializationIO once and passes that same adapter to plan_migration and commit_migration. Its closed v1 schema dispatch and exact-source validation remain unchanged.
